facts.text: The FeCoNiTi alloy was rapidly quenched by arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth to stabilize an fcc+C14 dual-phase microstructure.
A compositionally matched, C14-dominant Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 alloy was synthesized as a phase-specific comparator.
Magnetic measurements on the alloys were performed at temperatures up to 400 K.
Spin-polarized density-of-states calculations were used to examine the electronic structures of the fcc and C14 phases.
The magnetic behavior was mediated by coexistence of a ferromagnetic fcc phase and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
Chemical partitioning produced an fcc phase of approximately Fe21.3Co24.8Ni32.2Ti21.6 and a C14 phase of approximately Fe27.3Co26.6Ni17.4Ti28.7.
Antiferromagnetic coupling between the Fe/Co/Ni and Ti sublattices reduced the saturation magnetization.
In the dual-phase structure, the fcc orbital moment, C14 phase, and spin-canted components promoted domain-wall pinning and increased coercivity.
The 1084 K and 168 K magnetic transitions were assigned to the fcc phase, whereas the 214 K transition was assigned to the C14 phase.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy exhibited three ferromagnetic transitions at 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
The dual-phase alloy had a coercive field substantially higher than the approximately 100 Oe upper limit of the single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
The reported coercive field was approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
